links.comparator_used: No alternative arm; performance of the initial AI version at first calibration test compared with later versions re-tested after each architectural update
links.outcome: Diagnostic performance (AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) across seven repeated calibration tests, with the fixed 100-case set rerun after architectural updates
links.effect: Over the testing and monitoring period AUC rose from 0.83 to 0.92, accuracy from 0.77 to 0.90, sensitivity from 0.84 to 0.88 and specificity from 0.70 to 0.91. Calibration tests 1 and 2 failed the predefined thresholds, test 3 passed, and test 6 failed again (accuracy 0.81, sensitivity 0.81, specificity 0.81; relative deviation about 11-12%). Test 7 passed (AUC 0.92, accuracy 0.90).
links.tradeoff: The calibration set was small (100 mammograms) and there was no external validation. The design cannot isolate the effect of specific updates from concurrent changes in data distribution and workflow, so gains cannot be attributed solely to the updates. No comparison against one-time validation was made.
links.quote: Gradual improvements in calibration testing post-AI updates highlight the importance of iterative optimization and continuous monitoring for mammography AI.

design_hint: lifecycle testing with prospective monitoring and calibration across updates
